Flash Floods Disrupt Hospitality Operators in Qatar as Storms Continue

A series of intense storms has caused severe flash flooding across parts of Qatar, forcing significant disruption at numerous hospitality industry sites and leaving many employees unable to work. The ongoing storms, which began on Sunday and have brought record rainfall to the region, have inundated resorts, hotels, and hospitality-operated recreational parks, with the extent of the damage still being assessed as authorities warn that further heavy rain is expected in the coming days.

According to the Qatar Hospitality Association, at least 16 hotel properties and three major resort complexes in and around Doha and Al Wakrah have reported flooding of guest areas, basement facilities, and staff accommodations. “The rainfall overwhelmed drainage systems designed for normal seasonal conditions, leading to rapid water buildup in lower floors and service areas,” said Hassan Al-Naemi, the association’s spokesperson. “Our members are facing significant challenges in maintaining operations, ensuring guest safety, and protecting workers’ welfare.”

Multiple hospitality companies have temporarily closed affected sites, relocating guests where possible and sending non-essential staff home. Staff who remain on site are working double shifts to mitigate water damage and maintain essential services. “We have over 140 employees impacted at our Al Rayyan facility alone, with 60 having to be evacuated from staff housing due to rising water,” said Fatima Al-Kuwari, operations manager at Desert Pearl Hospitality. “Many are concerned about their personal safety as well as the longer-term impact on their jobs.”

Industry analysts expect that the immediate costs of the flooding will be substantial. “Hospitality operators in Qatar are facing high expenses for emergency clean-up, loss of revenue from closed facilities, and the need for urgent repairs,” noted Khalid Sharif, an independent sector consultant. “The situation remains fluid, and we anticipate more sites may be affected if the heavy rains continue.”

The Hospitality Workers Union of Qatar has called on companies to provide temporary accommodation for displaced staff and to guarantee continued wages while sites are closed. “Our members are vital to the operation of these properties. Their safety and livelihoods must be protected,” said union president Mariam Al-Jaber.

With meteorologists forecasting continued storms through the weekend, the hospitality industry is bracing for further disruption and potential damage as it works to respond to the ongoing emergency.
